<a id="scheme-selection-framework"></a>

## Commercial model selection framework

Scheme `selection_framework`.

<a id="self-01"></a>

**SELF-01** Characterize the service (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Repeatability, scope, regulatory status, required expertise, locations and SLA.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 1

<a id="self-02"></a>

**SELF-02** Identify economic drivers (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Labor hours, unit volumes, complexity, fixed capacity, technology, subcontractors.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 2

<a id="self-03"></a>

**SELF-03** Quantify uncertainty (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Volume distribution, complexity variance, productivity, wage inflation, technology cost.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 3

<a id="self-04"></a>

**SELF-04** Identify client preferences (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Budget certainty, flexibility, transparency, avoidance of unused commitment.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 4

<a id="self-05"></a>

**SELF-05** Determine feasible billing bases (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Time, resource, capacity, output, usage, fixed, outcome.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 5

<a id="self-06"></a>

**SELF-06** Select compatible levers (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Commitment, collar, overage, service credit, indexation, rollover.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 6

<a id="self-07"></a>

**SELF-07** Screen regulatory and contract constraints (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Screen the candidate structures against regulatory and contractual constraints.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 7

<a id="self-08"></a>

**SELF-08** Model economics (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Model low, base and high cases and probabilistic economics.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 8

<a id="self-09"></a>

**SELF-09** Assess client value (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Effective unit cost, unused entitlement, cycle time, quality, avoided alternatives.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 9

<a id="self-10"></a>

**SELF-10** Compare candidates (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Compare candidate structures rather than forcing one optimum.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 10

<a id="self-11"></a>

**SELF-11** Identify negotiation exchanges (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Identify concessions that can be exchanged across dimensions.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 11

<a id="self-12"></a>

**SELF-12** Recommend alternatives (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Recommend alternatives with explicit assumptions and human-review triggers.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: order: 12

<a id="scheme-selection-heuristics"></a>

## Decision matrix heuristics

Scheme `selection_heuristics`.

<a id="sel-001"></a>

**SEL-001** Highly uncertain scope (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Decision-matrix heuristic for engagements characterized by: highly uncertain scope.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: characteristic: Highly uncertain scope; favored: Time and materials, Capped time and materials, Phased fee, Cost-plus; caution: Unlimited fixed fee; favored_refs: PM-001, PM-020, PM-017, PM-019; profile_signal: {"equals": "UNKNOWN", "path": "volume.certainty"}
- Caveat: Advisory heuristic; never used to rank or choose structures.

<a id="sel-002"></a>

**SEL-002** Stable high-volume repetitive work (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Decision-matrix heuristic for engagements characterized by: stable high-volume repetitive work.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: characteristic: Stable high-volume repetitive work; favored: Unit pricing, Fixed managed service, Subscription, Base plus variable; caution: Pure hourly if automation is expected to increase materially; favored_refs: PM-011, PM-007, PM-010, PM-023; caution_refs: PM-001; profile_signal: {"all": [{"equals": "KNOWN", "path": "volume.certainty"}, {"equals": "COUNT", "path": "unit_of_work.kind"}]}
- Caveat: Advisory heuristic; never used to rank or choose structures.

<a id="sel-003"></a>

**SEL-003** Dedicated ongoing team required (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Decision-matrix heuristic for engagements characterized by: dedicated ongoing team required.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: characteristic: Dedicated ongoing team required; favored: FTE or capacity reservation, Fixed managed service; caution: Pure per-unit pricing without a minimum if staffing cannot flex; favored_refs: PM-004, PM-009, PM-007; caution_refs: PM-011; profile_signal: {"equals": true, "path": "cost_profile.fixed_team"}
- Caveat: Advisory heuristic; never used to rank or choose structures.

<a id="sel-004"></a>

**SEL-004** Highly variable demand with pooled capacity (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Decision-matrix heuristic for engagements characterized by: highly variable demand with pooled capacity.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: characteristic: Highly variable demand with pooled capacity; favored: Per-unit, Consumption, Base plus overage; caution: Large take-or-pay commitment without rollover or flexibility; favored_refs: PM-011, PM-013, PM-023; caution_refs: PM-034; profile_signal: {"all": [{"in": ["RANGE", "UNKNOWN"], "path": "volume.certainty"}, {"not": {"equals": true, "path": "cost_profile.fixed_team"}}]}
- Caveat: Advisory heuristic; never used to rank or choose structures.

<a id="sel-005"></a>

**SEL-005** Material setup or engineering investment (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Decision-matrix heuristic for engagements characterized by: material setup or engineering investment.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: characteristic: Material setup or engineering investment; favored: Implementation fee plus recurring, Multi-year commitment; caution: Month-to-month fee with no termination recovery; favored_refs: PM-029; profile_signal: {"equals": true, "path": "cost_profile.setup_investment"}
- Caveat: Advisory heuristic; never used to rank or choose structures.

<a id="sel-006"></a>

**SEL-006** Heterogeneous complexity (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Decision-matrix heuristic for engagements characterized by: heterogeneous complexity.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: characteristic: Heterogeneous complexity; favored: Complexity-weighted units, Bands, Hourly for exceptions; caution: Single unadjusted unit price; favored_refs: PM-015, PM-001; caution_refs: PM-011; profile_signal: {"exists": true, "path": "unit_of_work.tiers[*]"}
- Caveat: Advisory heuristic; never used to rank or choose structures.

<a id="sel-007"></a>

**SEL-007** Strong client budget-certainty preference (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Decision-matrix heuristic for engagements characterized by: strong client budget-certainty preference.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: characteristic: Strong client budget-certainty preference; favored: Fixed fee, Subscription, Capped hybrid; caution: Pure uncapped usage; favored_refs: PM-006, PM-010; caution_refs: PM-013; profile_signal: {"equals": "budget_certainty", "path": "client_priorities[*]"}
- Caveat: Advisory heuristic; never used to rank or choose structures.

<a id="sel-008"></a>

**SEL-008** Strong client flexibility preference (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Decision-matrix heuristic for engagements characterized by: strong client flexibility preference.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: characteristic: Strong client flexibility preference; favored: Usage, Pooled unit pricing, Low base plus overage; caution: Dedicated FTE or high minimum commitment; favored_refs: PM-013, PM-011, PM-023; caution_refs: PM-004; profile_signal: {"equals": "pay_for_use", "path": "client_priorities[*]"}
- Caveat: Advisory heuristic; never used to rank or choose structures.

<a id="sel-009"></a>

**SEL-009** Measurable cost savings (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Decision-matrix heuristic for engagements characterized by: measurable cost savings.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: characteristic: Measurable cost savings; favored: Gain-share plus baseline and governance; caution: Pure gain-share with disputed counterfactual; favored_refs: PM-026; caution_refs: PM-026
- Caveat: Advisory heuristic; never used to rank or choose structures.

<a id="sel-010"></a>

**SEL-010** AI lowers human time sharply (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Decision-matrix heuristic for engagements characterized by: aI lowers human time sharply.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: characteristic: AI lowers human time sharply; favored: Output, Fixed, Platform plus service, Outcome, Usage; caution: Hourly-only if value remains constant; favored_refs: PM-011, PM-006, PM-028, PM-024, PM-030; caution_refs: PM-001; profile_signal: {"equals": true, "path": "flags.automation_expected"}
- Caveat: Advisory heuristic; never used to rank or choose structures.

<a id="sel-011"></a>

**SEL-011** Material regulatory continuity requirement (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Decision-matrix heuristic for engagements characterized by: material regulatory continuity requirement.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0004](#clm-b-0004)
- Attributes: characteristic: Material regulatory continuity requirement; favored: Reserved capacity, Dedicated or hybrid delivery, Robust exit provisions; caution: Extremely lean on-demand pool without continuity guarantees; favored_refs: PM-009, PM-004; profile_signal: {"equals": true, "path": "flags.continuity_required"}
- Caveat: Advisory heuristic; never used to rank or choose structures.

## Realizations

How each pricing model and lever becomes engagement terms in a structure proposal. Labels say who absorbs a deviation (D_PROPOSED); effects say how a lever changes them.

| Realization | Kind | Applies to | Labels or effects |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CL-R01](#cl-r01) `CL-R01` Minimum spend commitment | lever | variable | volume_shortfall: PROVIDER to SHARED, NONE_ADVERSE to SHARED |
| [CL-R06](#cl-r06) `CL-R06` Rollover of unused allowance | lever | allowance | volume_shortfall: CLIENT to SHARED |
| [CL-R09](#cl-r09) `CL-R09` Setup or onboarding fee | lever | any | early_exit: PROVIDER to SHARED |
| [CL-V04](#cl-v04) `CL-V04` Volume discount above a threshold | lever | variable | none |
| [CL-V05](#cl-v05) `CL-V05` Volume rebate | lever | variable | none |
| [CL-V07](#cl-v07) `CL-V07` Annual fee cap | lever | unit_priced | spend_variability: VARIABLE to BOUNDED; volume_excess: NONE_ADVERSE to PROVIDER |
| [CL-V08](#cl-v08) `CL-V08` Volume collar | lever | unit_priced | volume_shortfall: PROVIDER to SHARED, NONE_ADVERSE to SHARED; volume_excess: NONE_ADVERSE to SHARED |
| [CL-P01](#cl-p01) `CL-P01` Service-level credit | lever | any | none |
| [CL-P02](#cl-p02) `CL-P02` Performance bonus | lever | any | none |
| [CL-P12](#cl-p12) `CL-P12` Annual indexation | lever | any | none |
| [CL-P14](#cl-p14) `CL-P14.fee` Termination fee | lever | any | early_exit: PROVIDER to CLIENT, SHARED to CLIENT, NONE_ADVERSE to CLIENT |
| [CL-P14](#cl-p14) `CL-P14.prorated` Prorated minimum on early exit | lever | minimum | early_exit: PROVIDER to SHARED, NONE_ADVERSE to SHARED |
| [PM-001](#pm-001) `PM-001` Hourly time and materials | model | HOURS | volume_shortfall: PROVIDER; volume_excess: NONE_ADVERSE; spend_variability: VARIABLE; mix: CLIENT |
| [PM-020](#pm-020) `PM-020` Capped time and materials | model | HOURS | volume_shortfall: PROVIDER; volume_excess: PROVIDER; spend_variability: BOUNDED; mix: PROVIDER |
| [PM-004](#pm-004) `PM-004` Dedicated team priced per FTE | model | COUNT, HOURS, FTE_MONTHS | volume_shortfall: CLIENT; volume_excess: PROVIDER; spend_variability: FIXED; mix: PROVIDER |
| [PM-007](#pm-007) `PM-007` Fixed-fee managed service | model | COUNT, HOURS | volume_shortfall: CLIENT; volume_excess: PROVIDER; spend_variability: FIXED; mix: PROVIDER |
| [PM-011](#pm-011) `PM-011` Per-unit pricing | model | COUNT | volume_shortfall: PROVIDER; volume_excess: NONE_ADVERSE; spend_variability: VARIABLE; mix: CLIENT |
| [PM-014](#pm-014) `PM-014` Volume-banded unit pricing | model | COUNT | volume_shortfall: SHARED; volume_excess: NONE_ADVERSE; spend_variability: VARIABLE; mix: CLIENT |
| [PM-015](#pm-015) `PM-015` Complexity-weighted unit pricing | model | COUNT (needs tiers) | volume_shortfall: PROVIDER; volume_excess: NONE_ADVERSE; spend_variability: VARIABLE; mix: CLIENT |
| [PM-023](#pm-023) `PM-023` Base fee with an allowance plus overage | model | COUNT, HOURS | volume_shortfall: CLIENT; volume_excess: NONE_ADVERSE; spend_variability: VARIABLE; mix: PROVIDER |

## Rules

<a id="compat-001"></a>

**COMPAT-001** `COMPAT_CAPACITY_PLUS_OVERAGE` (compatibility, INFO, evaluated)

Capacity reservation combined with usage overage is a structurally valid combination.

- Assessment: `STRUCTURALLY_VALID`
- Why: The base payment buys readiness and excess consumption can be separately metered; cloud commitment models demonstrate analogous economics.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-B-0008](#clm-b-0008), [CLM-B-0009](#clm-b-0009)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "all": [
  {
   "any": [
    {
     "path": "arrangement_versions[*].commitments[*].kind",
     "equals": "RESERVED_CAPACITY"
    },
    {
     "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].billing_basis",
     "equals": "CAPACITY"
    }
   ]
  },
  {
   "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].calculation_method",
   "equals": "ALLOWANCE_OVERAGE"
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="compat-002"></a>

**COMPAT-002** `COMPAT_FIXED_MANAGED_PLUS_SLA_CREDITS` (compatibility, INFO, evaluated)

A fixed-fee managed service with SLA credits is a structurally valid combination.

- Assessment: `STRUCTURALLY_VALID`
- Why: The base fee and the performance remedy address different dimensions.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "all": [
  {
   "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].calculation_method",
   "equals": "FIXED_RECURRING"
  },
  {
   "path": "arrangement_versions[*].adjustments[*].type",
   "equals": "SLA_CREDIT"
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="compat-003"></a>

**COMPAT-003** `COMPAT_FIXED_MANAGED_PLUS_BONUS` (compatibility, INFO, evaluated)

A fixed-fee managed service with a performance bonus is structurally valid if the bonus metric is measurable.

- Assessment: `STRUCTURALLY_VALID`
- Why: Fixed core economics are combined with an upside incentive; the metric must be measurable.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "all": [
  {
   "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].calculation_method",
   "equals": "FIXED_RECURRING"
  },
  {
   "path": "arrangement_versions[*].adjustments[*].type",
   "equals": "BONUS"
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="compat-004"></a>

**COMPAT-004** `COMPAT_UNIT_PLUS_COMPLEXITY` (compatibility, INFO, evaluated)

Complexity-adjusted unit pricing is conditionally preferred where unit cost variance is material and objectively classifiable.

- Assessment: `CONDITIONALLY_PREFERRED`
- Why: Appropriate where unit cost variance is material and objectively classifiable.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-B-0051](#clm-b-0051)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "any": [
  {
   "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].calculation_method",
   "equals": "WEIGHTED_UNIT_OUTPUT"
  },
  {
   "path": "descriptors.rate_structure",
   "equals": "COMPLEXITY_WEIGHTED"
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="compat-005"></a>

**COMPAT-005** `COMPAT_COMMITMENT_PLUS_ROLLOVER` (compatibility, WARNING, evaluated)

A minimum commitment with rollover defers the delivery obligation; review future capacity concentration.

- Assessment: `STRUCTURALLY_VALID_BUT_LIABILITY_SHIFTING`
- Why: Rollover improves fairness but defers the delivery obligation and can cause future capacity concentration.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "all": [
  {
   "path": "arrangement_versions[*].commitments[*].kind",
   "in": [
    "MINIMUM_SPEND",
    "MINIMUM_VOLUME"
   ]
  },
  {
   "path": "arrangement_versions[*].entitlements[*].rollover.policy",
   "in": [
    "NEXT_PERIOD",
    "TERM"
   ]
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="compat-006"></a>

**COMPAT-006** `COMPAT_COMMITMENT_PLUS_TRANSFERABLE_CREDITS` (compatibility, INFO, evaluated)

A commitment with credits transferable across a service catalog is a structurally valid combination.

- Assessment: `STRUCTURALLY_VALID`
- Why: Demonstrated by at least one provider's multi-service credit subscription.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "all": [
  {
   "path": "arrangement_versions[*].commitments[*].kind",
   "equals": "PREPAID_CREDIT"
  },
  {
   "path": "descriptors.scope",
   "equals": "CATALOG"
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="compat-007"></a>

**COMPAT-007** `COMPAT_GAIN_SHARE_VS_BUDGET_CERTAINTY` (compatibility, WARNING, not evaluated)

Gain-share conflicts with strict budget predictability unless the outcome-dependent amount is capped.

- Assessment: `ECONOMICALLY_CONFLICTING`
- Why: Outcome-dependent consideration creates variability unless capped.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-B-0006](#clm-b-0006)

**COMPAT-008** `COMPAT_OUTCOME_FEE_UNMEASURABLE_RESULT` (compatibility, WARNING, not evaluated)

An outcome fee tied to an unmeasurable business result is structurally weak.

- Why: Baseline, attribution and controllability problems make enforcement and economics uncertain.

- Claims: [CLM-B-0041](#clm-b-0041)

Guaranteed capacity is present; reserved delivery cost may persist even if consumption is zero.

**RULE-002** `RULE_COMPLEXITY_NORMALIZATION` (reasoning, WARNING, not evaluated)

Unit cost appears to vary by complexity; unadjusted unit pricing can create adverse-selection or margin risk.

- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-B-0051](#clm-b-0051)

**RULE-003** `RULE_INCENTIVE_PREREQUISITES` (reasoning, WARNING, evaluated)

Pooled delivery is declared; under low client demand the provider may redeploy resources, so incremental cost can fall further than under a dedicated model.

**RULE-013** `RULE_ADVANCE_BILLING_NOT_REVENUE` (reasoning, INFO, not evaluated)

Revenue billed in advance does not automatically equal recognized revenue.

**RULE-015** `RULE_SAVINGS_CLAIM_TOTAL_COST` (reasoning, WARNING, not evaluated)

A savings claim should include transition, technology, governance and QA costs before total economics are compared.

- Why: When a provider claims savings, transition, technology, governance and QA costs should be included before comparing total economics.

## Claims

| Claim | Statement | Evidence | Prevalence | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="clm-b-0001"></a>CLM-B-0001 | An actual commercial arrangement is better represented as a composition of billing basis, rate structure, commitment, risk allocation, adjustment mechanisms and delivery obligations than as a single pricing model. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0002"></a>CLM-B-0002 | Billing bases are not mutually exclusive: managed services and capacity reservations combine recurring, output, capacity and usage elements in one arrangement. | B_CORROBORATED | ESTABLISHED_COMMON | [E020](#e020), [E023](#e023) |
| <a id="clm-b-0003"></a>CLM-B-0003 | Many apparently innovative commercial structures, including multi-year subscriptions, committed consumption, output pricing, service credits, shared savings and capacity reservation, adapt older outsourcing and professional-services mechanisms. | B_CORROBORATED | ESTABLISHED_COMMON | [E020](#e020), [E021](#e021), [E023](#e023) |
| <a id="clm-b-0004"></a>CLM-B-0004 | Commercial structure selection is a multi-objective decision problem with rarely one uniquely optimal structure absent assumptions about volume, cost behavior, preferences, risk tolerance, capacity and renewal economics. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0005"></a>CLM-B-0005 | At least one large advisory firm describes its managed services as multi-year as-a-service subscriptions with predictable cost and outcome-oriented service levels. | A_DIRECT | ESTABLISHED_COMMON | [E020](#e020) |
| <a id="clm-b-0006"></a>CLM-B-0006 | Outcome-based outsourcing guidance describes linking provider compensation to operational results, cost-saving targets and productivity glide paths. | B_CORROBORATED | DOCUMENTED_SPECIALIZED | [E021](#e021) |
| <a id="clm-b-0007"></a>CLM-B-0007 | Managed-services contracting guidance for generative AI identifies shared cost savings, incentives, data ownership, AI alliances, SLAs and value tracking as commercial-contract considerations. | A_DIRECT | EMERGING | [E022](#e022) |
| <a id="clm-b-0008"></a>CLM-B-0008 | Cloud marketplace documentation describes committed-use pricing that combines a minimum commitment with usage and overage charges. | A_DIRECT | ESTABLISHED_COMMON | [E023](#e023) |
| <a id="clm-b-0009"></a>CLM-B-0009 | A large cloud provider's savings plans exchange a spend commitment for discounted rates, with usage above the commitment charged at on-demand rates. | A_DIRECT | ESTABLISHED_COMMON | [E024](#e024) |
| <a id="clm-b-0010"></a>CLM-B-0010 | A large cloud provider's savings plans commit the customer to hourly spend regardless of actual usage. | A_DIRECT | ESTABLISHED_COMMON | [E025](#e025) |
| <a id="clm-b-0011"></a>CLM-B-0011 | IFRS 15 requires identifying the contract and its performance obligations, determining and allocating the transaction price, and recognizing revenue when or as obligations are satisfied. | A_DIRECT | ESTABLISHED_COMMON | [E026](#e026) |
| <a id="clm-b-0012"></a>CLM-B-0012 | ASC Topic 606 establishes the analogous US GAAP revenue-recognition framework. | A_DIRECT | ESTABLISHED_COMMON | [E027](#e027) |
| <a id="clm-b-0013"></a>CLM-B-0013 | Revenue recognition under IFRS 15 and ASC Topic 606 is based on performance obligations and transfer of promised services, not invoice timing or receipt of cash. | A_DIRECT | ESTABLISHED_COMMON | [E026](#e026), [E027](#e027) |
| <a id="clm-b-0014"></a>CLM-B-0014 | One professional-services software vendor defines project gross margin as revenue less labor and direct or reimbursable expenses where overhead is not allocated. | A_DIRECT | DOCUMENTED_SPECIALIZED | [E038](#e038) |
| <a id="clm-b-0015"></a>CLM-B-0015 | The UK financial conduct regulator states that firms remain responsible for managing third-party and outsourcing risk; its July 2026 update to that guidance concerns critical third parties. | A_DIRECT | UNVERIFIED | [E032](#e032) |
| <a id="clm-b-0016"></a>CLM-B-0016 | The UK financial conduct regulator finalized material third-party reporting rules in March 2026 that take effect on March 18, 2027. | A_DIRECT | UNVERIFIED | [E033](#e033) |
| <a id="clm-b-0017"></a>CLM-B-0017 | The March 2026 update to SS2/21 sets expectations on audit and access rights for material outsourcing arrangements from March 18, 2027. | A_DIRECT | UNVERIFIED | [E034](#e034) |
| <a id="clm-b-0018"></a>CLM-B-0018 | UK prudential outsourcing expectations address exit obligations for material outsourcing arrangements. | A_DIRECT | UNVERIFIED | [E034](#e034) |
| <a id="clm-b-0019"></a>CLM-B-0019 | UK data-protection guidance on AI contracts calls for documented controller and processor roles, due diligence, accuracy KPIs or SLAs, subprocessor controls, security measures, audit rights and end-of-contract data handling. | A_DIRECT | UNVERIFIED | [E035](#e035) |
| <a id="clm-b-0020"></a>CLM-B-0020 | UK financial-services AI good-practice material stresses third-party oversight, visibility into model changes, fallback arrangements, exit options and avoidance of untested vendor assurances. | A_DIRECT | UNVERIFIED | [E036](#e036) |
| <a id="clm-b-0021"></a>CLM-B-0021 | Fully loaded profitability and incremental contribution answer different questions: a renewal unattractive after overhead allocation may still have positive contribution, and a contributing contract may be unsustainable if the portfolio never covers shared costs. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0022"></a>CLM-B-0022 | Cost categories should not automatically share one allocation method; dedicated idle capacity and pooled portfolio capacity are treated differently. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0023"></a>CLM-B-0023 | Markup is (price - cost) / cost and margin is (price - cost) / price; conflating them is a material pricing error, and a 25% margin implies a 33.33% markup. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0024"></a>CLM-B-0024 | The minimum sustainable price under a target contribution margin is a decision formula, not a benchmark; the target margin and risk premium must come from internal governance. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0025"></a>CLM-B-0025 | A unit price derived at one forecast volume can become uneconomic at a lower realized volume because fixed cost is spread across fewer units. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0026"></a>CLM-B-0026 | Capacity-constrained cost should distinguish normal capacity from demand above it, so high volume is not assumed to be served indefinitely at the same marginal cost. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0027"></a>CLM-B-0027 | Monte Carlo simulation is an analytical extension that should not be mistaken for a prediction unless its distributions are empirically calibrated. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0028"></a>CLM-B-0028 | Margin-at-Risk can be defined as target contribution less a chosen quantile of contribution; it is a proposed management measure unless an organization defines it formally. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0029"></a>CLM-B-0029 | Client Value-at-Risk, a downside measure of realized value relative to committed spend, lacks sufficient public evidence to be treated as a validated metric. | D_PROPOSED | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0030"></a>CLM-B-0030 | AI-enabled services should be modeled as a production system with engineering, implementation, platform, infrastructure, inference, validation, exception, QA, monitoring, security, revalidation and migration costs, not as a zero-cost labor replacement. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0031"></a>CLM-B-0031 | There is no credible evidence of a universal automation-savings sharing percentage. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0032"></a>CLM-B-0032 | Pricing an automation-redesigned service by the remaining human hours prices the input that became scarce rather than the service delivered and could fail to recover technology investment. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0033"></a>CLM-B-0033 | Provider-retained automation benefit creates the strongest incentive to invest but may invite competitive repricing. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0034"></a>CLM-B-0034 | Client-retained automation benefit accelerates adoption but can make provider investment unattractive. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0035"></a>CLM-B-0035 | Shared automation benefit can align incentives but increases measurement complexity. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0036"></a>CLM-B-0036 | Productivity glide paths that pass efficiencies through on a contractual schedule have direct precedent in broader outsourcing and managed services. | B_CORROBORATED | DOCUMENTED_SPECIALIZED | [E021](#e021), [E022](#e022) |
| <a id="clm-b-0037"></a>CLM-B-0037 | Bundling technology and service suits a client wanting one business outcome where the provider controls the production stack; unbundling suits volatile consumption, transparency needs, portable licenses or material third-party model costs. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0038"></a>CLM-B-0038 | Not all client value components are readily monetizable: avoided cost needs a credible counterfactual, risk reduction is probabilistic, availability may never be used, and quality needs normalized defect definitions. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
| <a id="clm-b-0039"></a>CLM-B-0039 | Commercial-health indicators are management indicators, not validated industry thresholds. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |

| <a id="clm-b-0043"></a>CLM-B-0043 | Tiered pricing, not-to-exceed, minimum commitment, subscription, managed service, technology-enabled service, SLA credits, performance bonuses, complexity weighting and portfolio pricing are better represented as modifiers or configurations than as independent pricing models. | C_INFERENCE | UNVERIFIED |  |
